newsitem.title: USA: W.African crudes drying up in US, N.Sea bbls scant.
newsitem.headline: W.African crudes drying up in US, N.Sea bbls scant.

text.p: A bevy of West African crude oil availabilities was seen drying up on Wednesday even as North Sea offerings remained scarce, traders said on Wednesday.
An East Coast refiner bought three Nigerian Qua Iboe cargoes from three different trading houses at 20-30 cents over dated Brent fob for the first, second and last decades of July, traders said.
The purchases helped to clear out some of the West African availabilities in the absence of North Sea barrels, traders said.

Brent crude was notionally assessed around 50 cents under West Texas Intermediate/Cushing on a delivered basis for July 10-15, although a bouncing transatlantic arbitrage made the price hard to pin down, traders said.
"The spread widened out this morning, then got crushed this afternoon," a Gulf Coast buyer said.
The July WTI/Brent spread was around $1.10-20 on Wednesday afternoon, down some 15 cents from midday.
"Right now, it's tough moving (North Sea) barrels in this direction," a Gulf Coast trader said. "There's not great demand here, but there's still core demand."
In Latin America, Colombia's state oil company Ecopetrol was tendering a Cano Limon cargo for July 20-31 loading, with bids due on Thursday.
A U.S. company was also offering a Cano Limon cargo for mid-July loading, asking around $2.50 under WTI/Cushing.
Closely watched Venezuelan Mesa-30 was assessed around WTI/Cushing minus $3.25 a barrel.
In Argentina, oil producers inked two new term contracts for Canadon Seco crude beginning in June, trade sources said.
Spain's Repsol signed a one-year deal with Brazil's state oil company Petrobras for 6,000 barrels per day (bpd), at WTI/Cushing minus $4.40 a barrel. The price could be revised in six months.
Separately, Argentine companies Compania Naviera Perez Companc, Bridas, Astra and Cadipsa signed a nine-month deal with Atlantic Richfield Co for around 13,000 bpd.
The ARCO deal was priced at $3.70 a barrel under WTI/Cushing.
